The Journey

Six steps to your family

Every journey moves at its own pace, and yours will be entirely your own. Most families welcome their baby 18–24 months after that first conversation. Here's what the road ahead looks like, so nothing feels uncertain.

Schedule a Consultation

  1. Consultation

    A private, unhurried conversation about your goals, timeline, and budget. No pressure, no obligation, just clarity.

  2. Match Preparation & Embryo Creation

    We coordinate with your fertility clinic (or refer you to trusted partners) while preparing your family profile for matching.

  3. Match with an Ideal Surrogate

    We present carefully considered matches from our top-2% surrogate pool. You meet, connect, and decide together.

  4. Preparing for Pregnancy

    Independent legal counsel for both parties, medical clearances, escrow, and insurance, all managed by our team.

  5. Pregnancy

    Regular updates, milestone celebrations, and dedicated support for you and your surrogate through all three trimesters.

  6. Delivery of Your Baby

    We coordinate the birth plan, hospital arrangements, and parentage documentation. We're beside you until you're home as a family.

Investment

Transparent from the first conversation

Surrogacy is a significant investment, and you deserve total clarity before you ever begin. We know firsthand how much weight these decisions carry, so every Ember journey comes with a detailed, line-item budget and no hidden fees, covering agency services, surrogate compensation, legal work, insurance, and escrow. Nothing buried, nothing to catch you off guard later.

In your very first consultation, we'll walk through a personalized estimate together and answer every financial question you have, honestly and without pressure.

Common Questions

Intended parent FAQs

How long does the surrogacy process take?

Most families welcome their baby 18–24 months after their first consultation. Timing depends on embryo readiness, matching, and medical schedules. Your case manager keeps you informed at every stage.

Do you work with LGBTQIA+, single, and international parents?

Absolutely! Ember proudly serves all paths to parenthood: LGBTQIA+ individuals and couples, single parents by choice, international parents, and families of every kind, from around the world.

How are your surrogates screened?

Fewer than 2% of applicants are accepted. Every surrogate completes medical evaluation, psychological screening, background checks, insurance review, and in-depth interviews before they're eligible to match.

Can we choose our surrogate?

Yes. Matching is always mutual. We present matches that fit your values and expectations, you meet and connect, and both parties choose to move forward together.

What if we live in another state or country?

We work with intended parents nationwide and internationally. We match you with surrogacy-friendly jurisdictions, and our team handles coordination wherever you're based.

How do surrogacy laws differ by state or country?

Surrogacy laws vary widely from one place to the next. Some states and countries fully support surrogacy agreements and parentage, while others limit or restrict them. We help you understand these differences and match you with the right jurisdiction, so your journey rests on solid legal ground wherever you begin.

Why choose a surrogacy agency instead of an independent journey?

An agency carries the parts that are difficult to manage alone: careful screening, thoughtful matching, legal coordination, escrow, insurance, and support at every step. An independent journey can work, but it leaves the risk and logistics on your shoulders. Ember gives you a dedicated team, so you can focus on the relationship and the baby to come.

Common Questions

Surrogate FAQs

Surrogacy basics

What is surrogacy?

A surrogate (or gestational carrier) carries a pregnancy for intended parents. With gestational surrogacy, an embryo made through IVF from the parents' or donors' eggs and sperm is transferred to the surrogate, who isn't genetically related to the baby.

Gestational vs. traditional surrogacy: what's the difference?

Traditional surrogacy uses the surrogate's own egg and is rare today. Ember works only with gestational surrogacy, so your eggs are never used.

Surrogacy laws by state

Each state sets its own surrogacy laws. Here's the general picture.

Surrogacy-friendly

Clear legal support, and parents can usually be named before birth.

California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, District of Columbia, Illinois, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, Vermont, Washington

Generally workable

Common and achievable, but details like marital status or the county can matter.

Most other states, including Florida, Georgia, Maryland, Massachusetts, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Virginia

Less friendly

Compensated agreements are limited or not enforced.

Arizona, Indiana, Louisiana, Nebraska

Laws change, and this is general information, not legal advice. Your attorney confirms the laws that apply to you before any match.

What makes a state surrogacy-friendly?

The law clearly allows compensated gestational surrogacy, lets intended parents be named legal parents before birth, and treats every kind of family equally.

Requirements

What are the requirements?

Age 21 to 42, at least one healthy full-term pregnancy and a child you're raising, a BMI of about 19 to 32, non-smoking, a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and a reliable support system. Not sure? Take the quiz anyway.

Why does BMI matter?

A healthy BMI helps IVF work and lowers pregnancy risks like gestational diabetes. It's about keeping you safe.

Can I be a surrogate if my tubes are tied?

Yes. The embryo is placed directly in the uterus, so a tubal ligation doesn't matter.

Is there a limit on prior births or C-sections?

Most clinics follow American Society for Reproductive Medicine guidance of no more than five prior deliveries and three C-sections. The clinic makes the final call.

Which vaccines do I need?

Clinics usually require immunity to measles, mumps, rubella, and chickenpox. Other vaccines vary by clinic and family, and we discuss them before you match.

Do I need a partner?

No, as long as you have people who can help with your kids, appointments, and recovery.

Why does my partner need a background check?

Adults in your home are part of your support system, so clinics and intended parents ask for one. It helps keep everyone safe.

Compensation and costs

How much do surrogates make?

Ember surrogates receive $70,000 to $100,000+ in base compensation, depending on your state, experience, and agreement, paid from independent escrow, plus the benefits listed above.

Will I pay for anything?

No. Medical care, travel, legal fees, and screening are covered.

Your journey

Who decides on my match?

You do, together with the intended parents. Matching is always mutual.

How long does matching take?

It varies, often a few weeks to a few months after screening. We match on values, not speed.

Do I need to live near Ember?

No. We work with surrogates across the U.S., and clinic travel is arranged and paid for.

What protects me if the intended parents back out?

Your signed agreement makes them legally and financially responsible for the baby, and funds sit in escrow before medications start. You're never left on your own.

Is it hard to say goodbye after delivery?

You know from day one that you're helping another family grow, and many surrogates find their deepest bond is with the parents. Our team is here for every feeling.

How is Ember different?

We're boutique: one dedicated case manager, a team that includes former surrogates, independent legal and escrow, and matching built on shared values.

Privacy Policy

How Ember Families LLC collects, uses, and protects the information shared with us.

Last updated: October 2026

Ember Families LLC, doing business as Ember Surrogacy (“Ember,” “we,” “us,” “our”) respects your privacy and is committed to protecting it. This Privacy Policy describes the information we may collect from you when you visit our website or use our services, and how we collect, use, maintain, protect, and disclose that information. Please read it carefully. If you do not agree with our practices, please do not use our website or services.

Information we collect

We generally collect information from you in three contexts:

Learning about us. When you complete a form to request more information about our services, we ask for basic contact details, such as your name, email address, and phone number, and, where relevant, similar details about your partner.

Screening and eligibility. When you request a consultation or complete our eligibility quiz so that we can assess whether you may qualify for our program, we collect additional information through our forms. For prospective surrogates this may include health, pregnancy, lifestyle, insurance, and residency information needed to evaluate eligibility.

Supporting your journey. If we agree to work together, we collect the further information necessary to provide or coordinate the medical, legal, insurance, and other services involved in your journey as an intended parent or surrogate.

You may browse the public areas of our site without providing personal information. We also automatically collect limited technical data, such as browser type, device information, and pages visited, to operate and improve the site.

How we use your information

We use the information we collect to respond to your inquiries and requests; to personalize and improve your experience and our website; to provide customer support; to send you relevant information and periodic emails you have requested; to verify your identity and evaluate your eligibility for our program; and to provide, coordinate, and facilitate the services you engage us for. We also use it to operate, secure, and improve our site and to meet our legal and regulatory obligations.

How we protect your information

We use a range of administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect your personal information when you provide, submit, or access it. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, so while we work to protect your information, we cannot guarantee absolute security. Where you are given or choose a password for any part of our site, you are responsible for keeping it confidential.

Cookies

We use cookies and similar technologies to operate the site, remember preferences, understand site traffic and interaction, and improve our offerings. You can control cookies through your browser settings; disabling them may affect some features.

For details on how we handle health information shared in our surrogate eligibility quiz, see our Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy.

How we share information

We do not sell, rent, or trade your personally identifiable information. We share it only with trusted service providers who help us operate our website, run our business, or serve you — and only where they agree to keep it confidential. For example, we may share information with providers that support our communications and marketing, partners who assist with screening and evaluation, and, once you are working with us, insurers, healthcare providers, attorneys, and others as needed to deliver your services. We may also disclose information when we believe it is appropriate to comply with the law, enforce our policies, or protect the rights, property, or safety of Ember or others. We may share aggregated or de-identified information that does not identify you.

Third-party links

Our site may link to third-party sites or services that have their own privacy policies. We are not responsible for their content or practices, and we encourage you to review their policies.

Children’s privacy

Our website and services are directed to individuals who are at least 18 years old. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If you believe a child has provided us information, please contact us so we can remove it.

Your California privacy rights

If you are a California resident, the California Consumer Privacy Act (as amended) gives you the right to know what personal information we collect, use, and disclose; to request access to or deletion of your personal information; to correct inaccurate information; and to opt out of any sale or sharing of personal information (note that we do not sell your personal information). We will not discriminate against you for exercising these rights. To make a request, contact us at info@embersurrogacy.com; we may need to verify your identity before responding.

Users outside the United States

We are based in the United States, and by providing information to us you consent to its transfer to, and processing in, the United States, where privacy laws may differ from those in your location. If you are in the European Economic Area, you have rights to access, correct, delete, object to, restrict, or port your personal data, and we rely on your consent, our contract with you, or our legitimate business interests as the basis for processing. To exercise these rights, contact us using the details below.

Data retention

We retain personal information for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes described in this Policy and to meet our legal, tax, and regulatory obligations. Retention periods vary by context: information from general inquiries is kept for a shorter period than information gathered during screening or during an active journey, which we may retain for the duration of our relationship and any ongoing support, after which it is deleted or de-identified unless a longer period is required by law.

Health Data Privacy

How Ember Families LLC collects, uses, and protects health information shared with us.

Last updated: October 2026

This Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy supplements our Privacy Policy. It explains how Ember Families LLC, doing business as Ember Surrogacy (“Ember,” “we,” “us”) handles “consumer health data” as defined by laws such as Washington’s My Health My Data Act, Nevada SB 370, and the Connecticut Data Privacy Act. Ember is not a healthcare provider and is not subject to HIPAA, but we treat the health information you share with care.

Health data we collect

When you complete our surrogate eligibility quiz, we collect your answers about your pregnancy and birth history (including how many births and C-sections you have had and whether your pregnancies were healthy and full-term), your height and weight (which we use to calculate your BMI), whether you have had weight-loss surgery, an eating disorder in the last five years, or a history of serious mental illness or suicidal thoughts, and whether you smoke, vape, or use illegal drugs or live in a smoke-free home. We collect this together with your name, date of birth, state, email address, and phone number, and your answers about citizenship, government assistance, criminal history in your household, transportation, and support at home.

Where it comes from

We collect this information only from you, directly, when you submit the quiz.

Why we collect and use it

We use it only to evaluate whether you may be eligible to become a surrogate with Ember and to contact you about your application. We do not use it for advertising, and we do not sell it.

Your consent

We collect this information only after you give separate consent on the quiz. You can withdraw your consent at any time by emailing info@embersurrogacy.com.

Who we share it with

We share it only with service providers that process it on our behalf to receive and store your application: our form-processing provider and our email and cloud storage provider. They may not use it for their own purposes. We do not share it with affiliates or any other third parties without your separate consent, unless required by law.

How long we keep it

We keep your quiz answers only for as long as we need them to evaluate your application, support your journey if we work together, and meet our legal obligations, as described in our Privacy Policy.

Your rights

You may ask us to confirm whether we hold your health data, to send you a copy, to tell you who we have shared it with, or to delete it. Email info@embersurrogacy.com with the subject “Health data request.” We may need to verify your identity, and we will respond within 45 days. If we decline your request, you may appeal by replying to our response. If we deny your appeal, you may contact your state Attorney General.
